title: Etaleness of a supplied finite depth-two extension on a smooth local scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring with closed point $a$ and depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $U\subset L$ be open, contain every point not lying over $a$, and have dense inverse image in the scheme-theoretic closed fibre $L_a$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $p:E\to L$ be a supplied finite morphism, etale upon restriction over $U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume depth $\mathcal O_{E,z}\geq2$ whenever $p(z)\notin U$. Then $p$ is etale everywhere. The statement asserts no existence of E and no construction of an extension.

source.place: Proof of Tag 0EYB after construction of Y; uniqueness and flat base change in Tag 0EY6(2),(a),(b); Tag 0EYA

proof.text: The depth condition on E and uniqueness in 0EY6(2) identify p with the canonical finite extension of p restricted to U. Smoothness, depth A at least two, and the flat local depth formula put the necessary depth bound on L outside U. This identifies flat base changes of p with the canonical finite extensions by 0EY6(a). Enlarge U to the target open over which p is etale; its complement remains contained in the closed fibre and nowhere dense there.

If the complement is nonempty, choose a closed point of it inside an affine closed-fibre chart. The residue-field extension is finite. Use 07NE to realize it by a finite flat local base change, then 057G to get an etale local slice and a section through the point. Complete a smooth affine chart in the section ideal; by 05D5 it is A[[x_1,...,x_d]], and Noetherian completion is flat. Fibre density excludes d = 0; for positive d the generic point of the special fibre maps into U. Apply 0EYA to the restricted cover on the completed chart. The unique finite extension with depth two along the complement in 0EY6(2) identifies its etale extension with the pullback of p. The completion is faithfully flat after localizing at the chosen point, so etaleness descends and contradicts membership in the complement. Hence p is etale on all of L. Empty E and U = L satisfy the conclusion without this contradiction step.
